chunks: He said: Abul Qasim Ja'far ibn Muhammad, may Allah have mercy on him, reported to me from his father, from Sa'd ibn Abdillah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Sa'id ibn Janah, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad, from Jabir ibn Yazid, who reported from Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir (peace be upon them both), from his forefathers (peace be upon them), from the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his progeny):
"Paradise remains forbidden for the Prophets until I have entered it, and remains forbidden for all the nations until the Shi'ah of us, the Ahlul Bayt, have entered."

key_terms.أهل البيت: Ahlul Bayt -- the People of the House, the Prophet's household including Ali, Fatima, Hasan, and Husain
key_terms.الجنة: Paradise (Jannah) -- the abode of the righteous in the afterlife
key_terms.شيعتنا: Our Shi'ah -- literally 'our partisans/followers', referring to the devoted followers of Ahlul Bayt

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet Muhammad say about Paradise and the Shi'ah of Ahlul Bayt?
ai.summary: The Prophet Muhammad (SAWW), as transmitted through the chain of Imams back to Imam al-Baqir (AS), declared that Paradise is reserved first for him among the prophets, and among all peoples, his Ahlul Bayt's followers (Shi'ah) will enter Paradise first. This hadith from al-Amali al-Mufid establishes the special eschatological status of both the Prophet and the Shi'ah of Ahlul Bayt, emphasizing the centrality of loyalty to the Prophet's household in the afterlife.
